chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a person in janabah sleeping in the mosque, and he said: "He performs wudu (ablution), and there is no harm in his sleeping in the mosque and passing through it."

key_terms.اَلْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity)
key_terms.اَلْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque as a sacred space with specific rulings
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah sleep in the mosque after performing wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a person in janabah in relation to the mosque. It states that if he performs wudu (ablution), there is no harm in his sleeping in the mosque and passing through it, indicating a specific juristic concession tied to ritual purity.
